name: Entropy Minimization
analogy: Think of it as a coach who grades the model on the bars with answers, and on the ungraded bars simply says: stop shrugging. Every ungraded bar where the model answers could be either side costs it a point, which pushes its dividing line into the empty gaps between clusters of bars instead of through the middle of a crowd.

steps.title: Train as usual on the labelled bars
steps.description: The model starts like any classifier: it is scored on how wrong it is on the bars with a known outcome, and it adjusts to reduce that error.
steps.inExample: 250 five-minute MNQ bars with a known 6-bar outcome train a small neural network, the same as any supervised run.

steps.title: Have the model score the unlabelled bars
steps.description: At every training step the model also gives a probability to a large batch of bars with no outcome. These answers are not checked against anything, because the outcome is unknown.
steps.inExample: 5,000 unlabelled bars are scored in each pass, and some come out near 50 percent while others come out near 80 or 20 percent.

steps.title: Measure how undecided each answer is
steps.description: Each answer gets an indecision score. A probability near 50 percent is maximally undecided, while one near 0 or 100 percent is decisive. This score is what entropy measures, in plain terms.
steps.inExample: An answer of 52 percent scores nearly the maximum indecision. An answer of 85 percent scores much lower.

steps.title: Add an indecision penalty to the training goal
steps.description: The model is penalized for indecision on the unlabelled bars, with a dial that sets how heavy the penalty is. The model can only reduce the penalty by moving its dividing line so that fewer bars sit near it.
steps.inExample: The penalty is weighted at 30 percent of the labelled error, so wrong calls on known bars still matter most.

steps.title: Update, repeat and check on later bars
steps.description: The model repeats the two-part training for many passes. It is checked on labelled bars from a later period, held out of training, because too heavy a penalty can make the model confidently wrong.
steps.inExample: Training stops after 40 passes, when the score on the held-out later month stops improving.

steps.title: Score new bars with the sharpened model
steps.description: The finished model gives probabilities for new bars. They tend to be more decisive than those of a model trained on the labelled bars alone, so they need a calibration check before being treated as true probabilities.
steps.inExample: The 10:50 bar is scored at 60 percent for closing higher.

useFor.task: Sharpening a classifier that has few labels
useFor.example: Training a direction classifier on MNQ 5-minute bars with only a few hundred outcome labels, using months of unlabelled bars to place its dividing line.

useFor.task: Adding a semi-supervised term to a neural network
useFor.example: Dropping the indecision penalty into an existing neural network training run without changing its structure.
Teaching a pattern classifier on a small set of labelled chart images and a large pile of unlabelled ones.
Listing bars that still score near 50 percent after training, since they sit in the crowded middle where no pattern separates up from down.

avoidWhen: The up and down bars overlap heavily, as price direction usually does; the assumption that a clean gap exists between them is then false, and the penalty teaches the model false confidence.
You will size trades from the probability itself; the model's sharpened outputs are not true probabilities, so a Calibrated Classifier step is needed on top.

example.scenario: A researcher has 5,250 five-minute MNQ bars, 250 with a known outcome: whether the close 6 bars (30 minutes) later was above that bar's close. A small neural network is trained with the indecision penalty and then scores the 10:50 bar.

input.summary: Labelled bars for the usual error, unlabelled bars for the indecision penalty, and one new bar to score.

fields.name: labelled bars
fields.meaning: Bars with a known outcome that drive the ordinary error.

fields.name: unlabelled bars
fields.meaning: Bars with no outcome that drive the indecision penalty.

fields.name: weight of the indecision penalty
fields.meaning: How heavily indecision on unlabelled bars counts, as a share of the weight on error for labelled bars.

fields.name: close of the 10:50 bar
fields.meaning: The price at which the bar to be scored closed.

fields.name: price change over the last 6 bars
fields.meaning: How far price fell over the previous 30 minutes.

fields.name: relative strength index, 14 bars
fields.meaning: A momentum reading from 0 to 100; under 30 is commonly read as oversold.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent five-minute bar.

output.summary: A probability for the bar and its indecision score.

fields.name: probability the close is higher 6 bars later
fields.meaning: The sharpened model's answer for the 10:50 bar.

fields.name: call
fields.meaning: The side the probability falls on when the dividing line is 50 percent.

fields.name: indecision score
fields.meaning: On a scale where 0 percent is a certain answer and 100 percent is a coin flip, a value near the top means the answer is only mildly decisive.

example.reading: 60 percent with a high indecision score is still a hesitant lean. Because the method rewards confidence, compare its probabilities to what actually happened on later folds before trusting any of them.
